statement_utf8:
Determine whether P = PSPACE, that is, whether every language decidable by a deterministic Turing machine in polynomial space is decidable by a deterministic Turing machine in polynomial time.

Source: [Walter S. Brainerd and Lawrence H. Landweber et al., Computability, Decidability, Complexity, third edition.](https://art.torvergata.it/bitstream/2108/32769/60437/ComputabilityDecidabilityComplexity.pdf).

Status Open P versus PSPACE remains open. Recent space simulations and fixed-exponent time lower bounds do not separate polynomial time from polynomial space; conditional equality implications are not unconditional resolutions. Status reviewed Sep 14, 2026

Listed by [ProofAtlas](https://www.proofatlas.ai/open-problems/#problem-p-versus-pspace). Status qualification is attributed to ProofAtlas; no full resolution is certified here.
technical_disposition: P versus PSPACE needs an unconditional polynomial-time/space class comparison. A fixed-exponent hierarchy or finite machine enumeration cannot settle the union over all exponents; no full route.

statement_utf8:
Determine the truth values of BOTH NP subseteq BQP and BQP subseteq NP for unrelativized, advice-free classes of total languages over {0,1}. NP consists of languages with polynomial-length binary witnesses and a deterministic polynomial-time verifier. BQP consists of languages decided by polynomial-time uniformly generated polynomial-size quantum circuits (a deterministic Turing machine outputs Q_n on 1^n), using Watrous's fixed Toffoli, Hadamard and phase-i gates with |0> ancillas and discarding, followed by a standard-basis output measurement. On every yes input acceptance is at least 2/3, and on every no input it is at most 1/3. No arbitrary real gate constants, advice or oracle are available. Establish equality, either proper containment, or incomparability.

Source: [John Watrous, Quantum Computational Complexity, arXiv:0804.3401v1; language questions corroborated by Scott Aaronson lecture notes.](https://arxiv.org/pdf/0804.3401v1).

Status Open Both unrelativized BQP/NP inclusions remain unresolved on the checked evidence. Random-permutation oracle separations do not settle the stated uniform total-language relationship. Status reviewed Sep 14, 2026

Listed by [ProofAtlas](https://www.proofatlas.ai/open-problems/#problem-bqp-versus-np). Status qualification is attributed to ProofAtlas; no full resolution is certified here.
technical_disposition: Both inclusions for uniform advice-free total languages are required. Oracle or promise-problem separations do not transfer; no unconditional route for either inclusion.

statement_utf8:
Determine whether NC equals P, where NC consists of decision problems solvable by uniform polynomial-size circuit families of polylogarithmic depth and P consists of decision problems solvable in deterministic polynomial time.

Source: [J. Heemstra, J. Martens, and A. Wijs, Evaluating Massively Parallel Algorithms for DFA Minimisation, Equivalence Checking and Inclusion Checking, Introduction (2026).](https://arxiv.org/abs/2508.20735).

Status Open NC versus P remains open with a dated exact-status-source warning. Recent cellular-automaton or restricted-model classifications do not separate the same ordinary language classes. Status reviewed Sep 14, 2026

Listed by [ProofAtlas](https://www.proofatlas.ai/open-problems/#problem-the-nc-versus-p-problem-for-efficient-parallel-computation). Status qualification is attributed to ProofAtlas; no full resolution is certified here.
technical_disposition: Uniform polynomial size and polylogarithmic depth must cover all P languages. A parallel algorithm for one P-complete-looking example is insufficient without completeness and reduction scope; no full route.

statement_utf8:
Exhibit a Boolean function family computable in deterministic polynomial time whose nonuniform De Morgan formula size is superpolynomial; equivalently, prove that P is not contained in nonuniform NC^1.

Source: [Gavinsky, Meir, Weinstein, and Wigderson, ECCC TR13-190, revision 11, 2017.](https://eccc.weizmann.ac.il/report/2013/190/revision/11/download).

Status Open P versus nonuniform NC^1 remains open with dated-source qualification. Formula-composition progress does not establish the required superpolynomial De Morgan formula lower bound and is not the separate uniform P versus union-NC problem. Status reviewed Sep 14, 2026

Listed by [ProofAtlas](https://www.proofatlas.ai/open-problems/#problem-p-versus-nc-1). Status qualification is attributed to ProofAtlas; no full resolution is certified here.
technical_disposition: Requires one P family with superpolynomial nonuniform De Morgan formula size. A polynomial lower bound or uniform separation misses the quantifier over all polynomial sizes; no route.

statement_utf8:
Determine the exact large-cardinal consistency strength of ZFC plus the Proper Forcing Axiom (PFA): identify its equiconsistency level by matching upper and lower consistency bounds.

Source: [Oberwolfach Report 2025/2, Equiconsistencies between strengthenings of PFA and strengthenings of supercompact cardinals](https://ems.press/content/serial-article-files/51347).

Status Open Open; the 2025 Oberwolfach report continues to identify the exact consistency strength of PFA as unresolved. Relative consistency from a supercompact cardinal is an upper bound, not an equiconsistency theorem for PFA. Status review date not recorded in this edition

Listed by [ProofAtlas](https://www.proofatlas.ai/open-problems/#problem-exact-consistency-strength-of-the-proper-forcing-axiom-pfa). Status qualification is attributed to ProofAtlas; no full resolution is certified here.
technical_disposition: Matching consistency lower and upper bounds for ZFC+PFA is required. Relative consistency from a supercompact only supplies one side; no finite certificate or tractable full mechanism.

statement_utf8:
In the uniform random 3-SAT model, choose a 3-CNF formula with n variables and m clauses uniformly from formulas whose clauses contain three distinct literals. Determine the exact constant r_3 such that, as n tends to infinity with m/n tending to r, satisfiability has probability tending to 1 for r < r_3 and tending to 0 for r > r_3.

Source: [I. Caragiannis, N. Gravin, and Z. Jiang, On the Satisfiability of Random 3-SAT Formulas with k-Wise Independent Clauses, LIPIcs ESA 2025, Article 103, Introduction.](https://drops.dagstuhl.de/storage/00lipics/lipics-vol351-esa2025/LIPIcs.ESA.2025.103/LIPIcs.ESA.2025.103.pdf).

Status Open Status review date not recorded in this edition

Listed by [ProofAtlas](https://www.proofatlas.ai/open-problems/#problem-exact-satisfiability-threshold-for-random-k-sat-for-small-k-k-3). Status qualification is attributed to ProofAtlas; no full resolution is certified here.
technical_disposition: Requires a limiting zero-one threshold and its exact constant for random 3-SAT. Small n counts or large-k formulas do not establish the fixed k=3 limit; no route.

statement_utf8:
For each integer n>=2, let C_DFT(n) be the minimum number of steps needed to compute every output of the unnormalized complex DFT y_j=sum_(l=0)^(n-1) exp(-2*pi*i*j*l/n)x_l, 0<=j<n. Initially available functions are input coordinates and scalar constants; each step adds one affine function lambda*f+mu*g from two previously available functions with arbitrary complex scalars. Assertion: there exist c>0 and N such that C_DFT(n)>=c*n*log(n) for all n>=N. No coefficient bound, conditioning or memory restriction is imposed beyond this two-input scalar-step model.

Source: [An Omega((n log n)/R) Lower Bound for Fourier Transform Computation in the R-Well Conditioned Model, v5 header24July2014; internal31October2018](https://arxiv.org/pdf/1403.1307v5).

Status Open Status review date not recorded in this edition

Listed by [ProofAtlas](https://www.proofatlas.ai/open-problems/#problem-unrestricted-linear-circuit-fft-lower-bound). Status qualification is attributed to ProofAtlas; no full resolution is certified here.
technical_disposition: Arbitrary complex coefficients are allowed at every affine gate. Bounded-coefficient determinant or well-conditioned bounds do not apply; no unrestricted n log n argument.

statement_utf8:
Determine whether an algorithm exists which, given the exact adjacency matrix of any nonempty finite simple graph G and an integer t>=1, halts and returns a rational a with |a-Theta(G)|<=2^(-t), where Theta(G)=sup_{m>=1} alpha(G^{boxtimes m})^(1/m), alpha is independence number and boxtimes is the strong graph product. No running-time bound is imposed.

Source: [Holger Boche and Christian Deppe, Computability of the Zero-Error Capacity of Noisy Channels, arXiv:2010.06873v3 (19 May 2024).](https://arxiv.org/html/2010.06873v3).

Status Open Status review date not recorded in this edition

Listed by [ProofAtlas](https://www.proofatlas.ai/open-problems/#problem-top500-omission-w050054-computability-of-the-shannon-capacity-of-finite-graphs). Status qualification is attributed to ProofAtlas; no full resolution is certified here.
technical_disposition: Uniform terminating rational approximation for every finite graph and precision is required. Strong-power independence numbers supply lower approximations without an effective matching modulus; no algorithm or undecidability reduction.

statement_utf8:
Let t be a fixed transcendental indeterminate and C(t) the field of complex rational functions. Determine whether there exists an algorithm (Turing machine) which, given any n >= 1 and any polynomial f in Z[t][x_1,...,x_n], presented by its finite list of integer coefficients and monomial exponents in t and the x_i, halts and correctly decides whether f = 0 has a solution (x_1,...,x_n) in C(t)^n. Equivalently, determine whether the existential (positive existential) theory of the structure (C(t); 0, 1, +, -, *, t), with a constant symbol naming t and no constants for other complex numbers, is decidable. Inputs with arbitrary complex coefficients, and the ring language without a symbol for t, are not part of this target.

Source: [B. Poonen, Hilbert's tenth problem over rings of number-theoretic interest, Arizona Winter School notes, 2003.](https://math.mit.edu/~poonen/papers/aws2003.pdf).

Status Open Status review date not recorded in this edition

Listed by [ProofAtlas](https://www.proofatlas.ai/open-problems/#problem-provisional-top500-omission-waves-010-014.018). Status qualification is attributed to ProofAtlas; no full resolution is certified here.
technical_disposition: Named t and integer-coefficient inputs are essential. Algebraic closure of C does not make C(t) algebraically closed, and a result without named t has the wrong language; no decision or undecidability route.

statement_utf8:
Let $S$ denote the stack-sorting operator, let $\mathbf{i}$ denote the identity map, and let $\operatorname{des}$, $\operatorname{lmax}$, and $\operatorname{comp}$ be the descent, left-to-right maximum, and component statistics, respectively. Write $\operatorname{Id}(S\circ\mathbf{i}\circ S)$ for the set of permutations sorted by $S\circ\mathbf{i}\circ S$, and let Baxter permutations be the permutations in the corresponding Baxter class. **Distribution conjecture.** The triple of statistics

$$
(\operatorname{des},\operatorname{lmax},\operatorname{comp})
$$

has the same distribution on $\operatorname{Id}(S\circ\mathbf{i}\circ S)$ and on the set of Baxter permutations. This refines the enumeration result that $\operatorname{Id}(S\circ\mathbf{i}\circ S)$ is enumerated by the Baxter numbers; the conjecture was stated as a work in progress in the source.
technical_disposition: All lengths and the joint three-statistic distribution are required. Literal i is called identity, so SIS becomes S squared; Baxter enumeration then signals a source-map issue. No wording correction credited; source and successor bodies unread.

statement_utf8:
Let $P$ be a connected $d$-complete poset with maximum element $v_0$, rank function $r:P\to\mathbb{N}$, top tree $T$, and $d$-complete coloring $c:P\to T$. Let $\widehat P=P\sqcup\{\widehat1\}$ be obtained by adjoining a maximum element $\widehat1$ covering $v_0$, with extended coloring $\widehat c:\widehat P\to T\sqcup\{\widehat1\}$. For a $P$-partition $\pi\in\mathrsfs{A}(P)$, let $\widehat\pi$ extend $\pi$ by $\widehat\pi(\widehat1)=0$, and define $W_P(\pi;q,t)$ by

$$
W_{P}(\pi;q,t)
=\frac{\displaystyle
\prod_{{x,y\in\widehat P}\atop{x<y,\ \widehat c(x)\sim \widehat c(y)}}
f(\pi(x)-\pi(y);d(x,y))
}{\displaystyle
\prod_{{x,y\in P}\atop{x<y,\ c(x)=c(y)}}
f(\pi(x)-\pi(y);e(x, y))
f(\pi(x)-\pi(y);e(x, y)-1)
},
$$

where $d(x,y)=(r(y)-r(x)-1)/2$ and $e(x,y)=(r(y)-r(x))/2$. Here $\widehat c(x)\sim\widehat c(y)$ means that the colors are adjacent in the top tree. **Okada's $(q,t)$-hook formula conjecture.** Using these notations,

$$
\sum_{\pi\in{\mathrsfs{A}}(P)} W_{P}(\pi;q,t)z^{\pi} =F\left(z[H_{p}];q,t\right).
$$

This conjecture proposes a generating-function identity for weighted $P$-partitions of connected $d$-complete posets, extending the role of hook formulas in the theory of $P$-partitions. The supplied text gives no evidence of resolution, so its status remains open.
technical_disposition: Weighted identity for every connected d-complete poset needs the definitions of f, F, coloring and hooks. Proving ordinary hooks or a poset subclass is insufficient; no uniform mechanism.

statement_utf8:
Let $E_m$ be the $m\times m$ $(0,-1)$-matrix with $-1$s in positions $(2,m),(3,m-1),\ldots,(m,2)$, and let $F_m$ be the $m\times m$ $(0,-1)$-matrix with $-1$s in positions $(1,m-1),(2,m-2),\ldots,(m-1,1)$. For a matrix $A$, write $A\oplus B$ for its block direct sum, and let $I_1$ denote the $1\times 1$ identity matrix. **The extremal completion conjecture.** If $n\geq 4$ is even, then 
$$
E_{n/2}\oplus F_{n/2}
$$
 is the $n\times n$ bordered-permutation $(0,-1)$-matrix with the largest number of alternating sign matrix completions. If $n\geq 5$ is odd, then 
$$
E_{(n-1)/2}\oplus(-I_1)\oplus F_{(n-1)/2}
$$
 is the $n\times n$ bordered-permutation $(0,-1)$-matrix with the largest number of alternating sign matrix completions. The conjecture proposes an extremal structure for completions of bordered-permutation matrices; the supplied text gives no resolution, so its status remains open.
technical_disposition: Maximal ASM completion count among all bordered-permutation matrices for each n is required. Small transfer enumerations would be instances, without a compression monotonicity argument; no full route.

statement_utf8:
Let $G$ be a connected graph, let $
u_s(G)$ denote its induced matching number, let $n(G)$ denote its number of vertices, and let $C_5^2$ and $K_{3,3}^+$ be the two exceptional graphs described in the paper: $C_5^2$ is obtained from a $5$-cycle by replacing every vertex by an independent set of order $2$, while $K_{3,3}^+$ is obtained from $K_{3,3}$ by subdividing one edge once. Let $\Delta$ be the maximum degree of $G$.

**The induced matching bound.** If $G\notin\{C_5^2,K_{3,3}^+\}$ and $\Delta\geq 3$, then

$$
\nu_s(G) \geq \frac{1}{\left(\left\lceil\frac{\Delta}{2}\right\rceil+1\right)\left(\left\lfloor\frac{\Delta}{2}\right\rfloor+1\right)}n(G).
$$

The two excluded graphs show that the corresponding bound from the preceding theorem is not true for graphs of maximum degree $3$ or $4$ without exceptions. The conjecture asserts that these are the only exceptions.
technical_disposition: Induced matching bound applies to every connected graph with Delta>=3 except two explicit graphs. Greedy deletion loses the sharp approximately Delta squared/4 denominator; neither a sharper charging rule nor a counterexample is in hand.

statement_utf8:
A **groupoid term** is a term formed from variables using a binary operation $\star$. Two terms are **separated** in a groupoid if their interpretations can be made distinct under some assignment of the variables. The conjecture concerns pairs of terms that can be separated in an infinite groupoid.

**Finite separation conjecture.** Whenever two groupoid terms can be separated in an infinite groupoid, they can also be separated in a finite groupoid.

The claim would say that finite groupoids suffice to witness every separation of groupoid terms that is possible in an infinite groupoid. The examples preceding the conjecture construct finite separating groupoids for pairs of terms that are not covered by the preceding theorem, but the source gives no proof or resolution of the general statement.
technical_disposition: Primary v1 defines separation as inequality for ALL assignments, whereas corpus prose says some assignment. Conjecture 4.4 uses the universal definition. Finite term evaluation closure proves only the easy existential reading; reject that correction as credit. General universal finite separation remains HOLD.

statement_utf8:
Let $G$ be an abelian group of order $n$ and type $(n_1,\dots,n_r)$, and let $\rho_{\pm}(G,m,h)$ denote the minimum size of the $h$-fold signed sumset of an $m$-subset of $G$. Define $u_{\pm}(G,m,h)=\min\{f_d(m,h):d\in D(G,m)\}$, where $D(G,m)=\{d\in D(n):d=d_1\cdots d_r,\ d_1\in D(n_1),\dots,d_r\in D(n_r),\ dn_r\geq d_rm\}$. If there are odd divisors of $n$ greater than $2m$, let $d_m$ be the smallest such divisor. **The signed sumset minimum conjecture.** If $h\geq3$, then

$$
\rho_{\pm}(G,m,h)=u_{\pm}(G,m,h).
$$

If every odd divisor of $n$ is less than $2m$, then

$$
\rho_{\pm}(G,m,2)=u_{\pm}(G,m,2).
$$

If there are odd divisors of $n$ greater than $2m$, then

$$
\rho_{\pm}(G,m,2)=\min\{u_{\pm}(G,m,2),d_m-1\}.
$$

The conjecture proposes an exact formula for the minimum size of signed sumsets in finite abelian groups, refining the known lower and upper bounds and isolating the exceptional behavior at $h=2$.
technical_disposition: All finite abelian group types, subset sizes and h branches are required. Exact small sumset enumeration cannot resolve the general structural minimum; f_d and signed convention require primary definitions. No route.

statement_utf8:
Let $F$ be the nonarchimedean local field and let $G=\mathrm{SL}_\ell(F)$, with $\ell$ an odd prime. Let $T$ be an unramified torus, let $\psi\in\widehat{T(F)}$, and let $\gamma\in T(F)$ be regular. Write $r$ for the depth parameter of the representation associated with $\psi$, let $\gamma_{<r}$ denote the corresponding shallow component, let $X_{\psi,<d(\gamma)}^\ast$ be the associated truncated dual datum, let $D_G$ denote the discriminant, and let $\Gamma_{E/F}$ be the Galois group associated with the splitting field $E$ of $T$. 

**The conjectural character formula.** The character value is given by

$$
\Theta_\psi(\gamma)=|D_G(\gamma_{<r})|^{-\frac{1}{2}}|D_G(X_{\psi,<d(\gamma)}^\ast)|^{\frac{1}{2}}\epsilon_\psi(\gamma)\sum_{\sigma\in\Gamma_{E/F}}\psi(\gamma^\sigma),
$$

where $\epsilon_\psi(\gamma)$ is a root of unity depending on $\psi$ and $\gamma$.

This formula is intended to provide the character values on the unramified torus, where existing character formulas involving orbital integrals are difficult to compute. The paper indicates that the formula is conjectural because current techniques do not fully determine these values; in particular, a direct purely local proof of a key identity used in the torus character table remains to be found.
technical_disposition: All specified regular torus elements and characters require matching discriminants, depth truncations and epsilon. Local character expansion is not automatically the displayed exact formula; no full mechanism.

statement_utf8:
Let $G$ be a connected graph, and let $\Delta(G)$ and $\delta(G)$ denote its maximum and minimum degrees. A graph is **$\delta$-minimally** if it has the minimality property intended by the source. Its distinguishing index $D'(G)$ is the least number of labels in an edge labeling preserved only by the identity automorphism.

**Proposed distinguishing-index conjecture.** (i) If $G$ is a $\delta$-minimally graph with $\delta(G)\geq 3$ and $G$ is neither a complete bipartite graph nor a $\delta$-regular graph, then

$$
D'(G)\leq \left\lceil \sqrt[\delta(G)]{\Delta(G)}\right\rceil.
$$

(ii) If $G$ is connected and $\delta(G)\geq 3$, then

$$
D'(G)\leq 1+\left\lceil \sqrt[\delta(G)]{\Delta(G)}\right\rceil.
$$

The paper presents this as a conjecture because attempts to prove it had failed. The first part uses the source's term “$\delta$-minimally graph,” whose precise definition is not included in the supplied context.
technical_disposition: Part i has an undefined delta-minimal condition, and both degree bounds must be treated. A small graph violating an invented interpretation would not be a source counterexample; HOLD definitions and no route for ii.

statement_utf8:
Let $K=\mathbb{F}_q$ be a finite field, let $A_1,\ldots,A_s$ be subsets of $K$ defining a projective nested cartesian set

$$
\mathcal{X}=[A_1\times\cdots\times A_s],
$$

and write $d_i=|A_i|$ for $i=1,\ldots,s$. Let $C_\mathcal{X}(d)$ be the corresponding $d$-th projective nested cartesian code, and let $\delta_\mathcal{X}(d,1)$ denote its minimum distance. **Carvalho–Lopez-Neumann–López's minimum-distance conjecture.** The minimum distance is

$$
\delta_\mathcal{X}(d,1)=\left\{\hspace{-1mm} \begin{array}{ll}\left(d_{k+2}-\ell+1\right)d_{k+3}\cdots d_s&\operatorname{if} d\leq \sum\limits_{i=2}^{s}\left(d_i-1\right),\\
\qquad \qquad 1&\operatorname{if} d\geq \sum\limits_{i=2}^{s}\left(d_i-1\right)+1, \end{array} \right.
$$

where $0\leq k\leq s-2$ and $\ell$ are the unique integers such that

$$
d=\sum_{i=2}^{k+1}\left(d_i-1\right)+\ell
$$

and $1\leq \ell\leq d_{k+2}-1$. The statement was explicitly identified in the source as a conjecture, but the supplied material gives no resolution status; it is also immediately followed in the paper by a counterexample, so the status should be checked against that example.
technical_disposition: Corpus says the source gives a counterexample, but downloaded 1707.03285v1 is Generalized minimum distance functions and selected searches did not locate that conjecture/counterexample. No abstract-to-proof promotion: later-version/source fidelity remains HOLD; do not rediscover a claimed published example.

statement_utf8:
Let $\mathbb F$ be a finite field and let $\mathcal M$ be a proper minor-closed class of $\mathbb F$-represented matroids. An $\mathbb F$-represented matroid is a matroid with a fixed representation over $\mathbb F$; a represented frame matroid has a representation matrix with at most two nonzero entries per column; and a rank-$(\leq t)$ perturbation is obtained by adding a matrix of rank at most $t$ to a representation matrix.

**Perturbation conjecture.** There exist $k,t\in\mathbb Z_+$ such that each vertically $k$-connected member of $\mathcal M$ is a rank-$(\leq t)$ perturbation of an $\mathbb F$-represented matroid $N$ such that either $N$ is a represented frame matroid, $N^*$ is a represented frame matroid, or $N$ is confined to a proper subfield of $\mathbb F$.

This is the perturbation form of the announced structural result for highly connected representable matroids. The paper states that its dyadic examples provide a counterexample, so the conjecture is refuted.
technical_disposition: Primary Conjecture 1.2 and Corollary 3.7 give the exact obstruction for all k,t: dyadic examples are not bounded-rank perturbations of frame or dual-frame matroids; GF(3) has no proper subfield, defeating the third alternative. Existing theorem defeats eligibility. Full construction and dependency proof not audited.

statement_utf8:
Let $T^3$ denote the loose triangle in a triple system, and let the maximum degree of a triple system $G$ be the largest number of edges containing any fixed vertex. For a subgraph $H$ of $G$, write $e(H)$ for its number of edges and $e(G)$ for the number of edges of $G$.

**Sparse triple-system conjecture.** For $\triangle\geq 1$, there exists a triple system $G$ with maximum degree $\triangle$ such that, as $\triangle\to\infty$, every $T^3$-free subgraph $H$ of $G$ satisfies

$$
e(H)=o(\triangle^{-1/2})\cdot e(G).
$$

This would show that the lower bound for the size of a largest triangle-free subgraph is essentially sharp when $r=3$, up to the $o(1)$ term in the exponent. The surrounding discussion leaves the corresponding optimal exponent open for general $r$; the supplied status evidence concerns a different Kohayakawa–Łuczak–Rödl conjecture and does not resolve this one.
technical_disposition: Needs a family with every loose-triangle-free subgraph having an o(Delta^-1/2) fraction as Delta tends to infinity. A single finite graph or O(Delta^-1/2) bound is insufficient; no construction giving the little-o gain.

statement_utf8:
Let $n$ be the rank parameter of the type $B$ MultiTASEP, and write $\langle a,b\rangle$ for the two-point correlation of entries in the last two positions, with barred symbols denoting signed entries. The preceding text gives the identity $\langle i,\overline{j}\rangle=\langle i,j\rangle$. **Conjectured two-point correlations.** For the last two positions in the type $B$ MultiTASEP, the following identities hold:

$$
\langle \overline{i},\overline{j}\rangle=\frac{1}{(2n)^2}\quad (3\leq i\leq n,\ 1\leq j\leq i-2),
$$

$$
\langle \overline{j+1},\overline{j}\rangle=\frac{1}{(2n)^2}+\frac{n^2-j^2}{4n^2(2n-1)}\quad (1\leq j\leq n-1),
$$

$$
\langle \overline{i},\overline{j}\rangle=\frac{j-i}{2n^2(2n-1)}\quad (1\leq i\leq n-1,\ i+1\leq j\leq n),
$$

$$
\langle i,\overline{j}\rangle=\frac{i+j-1}{2n^2(2n-1)}\quad (1\leq i\leq n-2,\ i+2\leq j\leq n),
$$

$$
\langle j,\overline{j+1}\rangle=\frac{j(n^2-j^2+2n-2)}{2n^2(2n-1)(n-1)}\quad (1\leq j\leq n-1),
$$

$$
\langle i,\overline{j}\rangle=\frac{3(i-j)(i+j-1)}{4n^2(2n-1)(n-1)}\quad (2\leq i\leq n,\ 1\leq j\leq i-1).
$$

These formulas would determine all two-point correlations using the stated symmetry identity. The paper explains that its techniques do not determine all correlations, so these formulas are proposed as conjectural extensions of the proved results.
technical_disposition: All six probability identities across the given i,j,n ranges require the source Markov generator and stationary law. An isolated normalized table is not a stationary-distribution certificate; no uniform route.

statement_utf8:
Let $F$ be a totally real field, let $\mathfrak{n}$ be a nonzero ideal, let $F(\mathfrak{n})$ be its narrow ray class field, and let $H$ be the maximal CM subfield in which $\mathfrak{p}$ splits completely. Let $\pi$ satisfy $\mathfrak{p}^f=(\pi)$ as in the setup, let $\mathscr{D}$ be a Shintani domain, let $\mathbf{O}=\mathcal{O}_{\mathfrak{p}}-\pi\mathcal{O}_{\mathfrak{p}}$, and let $\nu(\mathfrak{b},\mathscr{D})$ be the associated measure. For the Frobenius element $\sigma_{\mathfrak{b}}\in\operatorname{Gal}(H/F)$, **Shintani's exact formula.** The associated conjugate of the Brumer–Stark unit satisfies

$$
\sigma_{\mathfrak{b}}(u_{\mathfrak{p}})=\epsilon(\mathfrak{b},\mathcal{D},\pi)\,\pi^{\zeta_{S,T}(F(\mathfrak{n})/F,\mathfrak{b},0)}\int_{\mathbf{O}}x\,d\nu(\mathfrak{b},\mathscr{D},x)\in F_{\mathfrak{p}}^*.
$$

This is the conjectural exact $p$-adic analytic formula proposed in the cited work; the source explains that a theorem relating the $p$-part of Gross's conjecture implies it up to a root of unity.
technical_disposition: Exact Brumer-Stark unit equality includes the root-of-unity factor. Equality modulo roots of unity does not settle this normalization; deep dependencies and no short full-scope mechanism.

statement_utf8:
Let $d\in\{1,2,3\}$. For each $n\ge 1$, let $\varphi_{n,L}$ be the corresponding eigenfunction, let $U_{n,L}\in[-L/2,L/2]^d$ be a point where $|\varphi_{n,L}|$ reaches its global maximum, and let $Q$ be the unique radial positive solution on $\mathbb R^d$ of

$$
-\Delta Q-Q^3=-Q.
$$

Set $a_L:= (C_d\log L)^{\frac1{2-\frac d2}}$ and $\psi_*(x):=Q(x)/\|Q\|_{L^2}$. **Eigenfunction localization conjecture.** For any $n\ge1$, the following convergence holds in probability as $L\to\infty$:

$$
\left(\frac1{a_L^{d/4}} |\varphi_{n,L}|\left(U_{n,L}+\frac{x}{\sqrt{a_L}}\right),x\in\mathbb R^d\right)\Rightarrow\psi_*;
$$

$$
\left(\frac1{a_L}\xi\left(U_{n,L}+\frac{x}{\sqrt{a_L}}\right),x\in\mathbb R^d\right)\Rightarrow-\frac{\psi_*^2}{\|\psi_*\|_{L^4(\mathbb R^d)}^2}\sqrt{\frac{2d}{C_d}}.
$$

This predicts that, after centering at a maximum and rescaling by the localization scale $a_L^{-1/2}$, every fixed eigenfunction has the universal profile $\psi_*$, while the rescaled noise converges to the corresponding squared profile. The source gives the optimizer characterization of $Q$ and the identity $\|Q\|_{L^4}^4=2d/C_d$, but does not state that this conjecture has been proved or refuted.
technical_disposition: Both rescaled eigenfunction and noise limits in probability for d=1,2,3 and each fixed n are required. Variational optimizer characterization alone is not stochastic localization; no full route or finite certificate.

statement_utf8:
A graph is **cyclically 4-edge-connected** if it has no cycle-separating edge-cut of fewer than four edges. A cubic graph has the **Perfect-Matching-Hamiltonian property** (PMH-property) if every perfect matching can be extended to a Hamiltonian cycle. The girth of a graph is the length of its shortest cycle, and the Heawood graph is the specified exception.

**Girth-at-least-six formulation of Funk et al.'s conjecture.** Every bipartite cyclically 4-edge-connected cubic graph with the PMH-property and girth at least $6$, except the Heawood graph, admits a perfect matching that can be extended to a Hamiltonian cycle in exactly one way.

The paper presents this as an equivalent way to search for a smallest counterexample to Funk et al.'s classification conjecture. It follows the observation that a smallest counterexample must be cyclically 4-edge-connected and have girth at least $6$; the supplied text gives no resolution.
technical_disposition: PMH and girth/connectivity hypotheses restrict every bipartite cubic graph. One matching uniquely extendible is existential within a universal graph claim; no structural reduction or certified exceptional graph found.

statement_utf8:
Let $k,n_1,n_2,n_3\ge 2$, and let $P_{n_1}\Box P_{n_2}\Box P_{n_3}$ be the three-dimensional grid graph. Write $\alpha_m(n_1,n_2,n_3)$ and $\alpha_M(n_1,n_2,n_3)$ for the quantities defined in the paper, and let $\dim_{k+1}$ denote the $(k+1)$-metric dimension.

**The conjecture.** If

$$
\alpha_m(n_1,n_2,n_3)\le k<\alpha_M(n_1,n_2,n_3),
$$

then

$$
\dim_{k+1}(P_{n_1}\Box P_{n_2}\Box P_{n_3})=\min\left\{4k-2\alpha_m(n_1,n_2,n_3)+4,\ n_1n_2n_3-(n_1-2)(n_2-2)(n_3-2)\right\}.
$$

The preceding results determine the exact value when $k<\alpha_m(n_1,n_2,n_3)$ and show that the displayed upper bound holds throughout the remaining range where a $(k+1)$-resolving set exists. The conjecture proposes the exact value in the intermediate range $\alpha_m(n_1,n_2,n_3)\le k<\alpha_M(n_1,n_2,n_3)$; when $\alpha_m=\alpha_M$, which occurs if $\min\{n_1,n_2,n_3\}=2$, the metric dimension is already completely determined.
technical_disposition: Source Conjecture 21 matches the intermediate range; alpha_m=2(n1+n2+n3)-8 and alpha_M=min ni(nj+nk-2). Source Propositions 17-18 handle k<alpha_m, not this range. Hitting constraints on all equidistance sets offer a finite-search encoding but no full sharp lower bound or witness; no sweep run, successor and registry HOLD.

statement_utf8:
Let $R$ be a finite principal ideal ring with identity, and let $\boldsymbol{I}_{\Psi}(\mathcal{S}_R)$, $\boldsymbol{D}_{\Psi}(\mathop{\rm U}(R))$, ${\rm Ind}(P)$, and ${\rm St}(P)$ denote the weighted Erdős–Burgess constant, weighted Davenport constant, index of a prime ideal, and stabilizer of that ideal under the action of $\Psi$, respectively. Let $\Psi$ be a subgroup of the group ${\rm Aut}(R)$.

**Weighted Erdős–Burgess equality conjecture.**

$$
{\rm I}_{\Psi}(\mathcal{S}_R)={\rm D}_{\Psi}({\rm U}(R))+\sum\limits_{P\in \operatorname{spec}(R)} \frac {T\left({\rm Ind}(P);\ \frac{|\Psi|}{|{\rm St}(P)|}\right)} {\frac{|\Psi|}{|{\rm St}(P)|}}.
$$

This conjecture asserts an exact formula for the weighted Erdős–Burgess constant of finite principal ideal rings, refining the preceding lower-bound conjecture. The source gives no evidence of resolution, so its status remains open.
technical_disposition: All finite principal ideal rings and automorphism subgroups require weighted sequence and T definitions. CRT alone does not automatically synchronize weights on factors; no exact extremal-sequence mechanism.

statement_utf8:
Let $L^2(\mathbb{R})$ be the Hilbert space of square-integrable functions, let $\mathcal{F}$ denote the Fourier transform, and let

$$
\mathcal{A}_{QM}=\left\{T:L^2(\mathbb{R})\rightarrow L^2(\mathbb{R},\mu)\mid T\text{ is unitary and }\mu\text{ is a Borel measure}\right\}.
$$

A tuple of measurement operators does phase retrieval if its associated measurement data determine a state up to the relevant phase equivalence. **Wright's conjecture.** There exists a unitary operator $T\in\mathcal{A}_{QM}$ such that $(\operatorname{Id},\mathcal{F},T)$ does phase retrieval.
This extends Pauli's phase-retrieval question by asking whether one additional unitary measurement, besides the identity and Fourier transform, suffices. The source attributes the conjecture to R. Wright and states that it remains open.
technical_disposition: Existence of a single extra unitary on L2(R) must separate every state modulo phase. Finite-dimensional generic measurements do not transfer without a global injectivity construction; no full route.

statement_utf8:
Let $G$ and $H$ be graphs, and let $G\square H$ denote their Cartesian product. For a vertex $u$ of a graph, let $\epsilon(u)$ be its eccentricity, let $\operatorname{d}(u,v)$ be the distance between vertices $u$ and $v$, and let $\operatorname{diam}(G\square H)$ be the diameter of the product. A pair of vertices is **almost peripheral** when $\epsilon(u)=\epsilon(v)=\operatorname{d}(u,v)<\operatorname{diam}(u,v)$. **Almost-peripheral-vertex conjecture.** If $G\square H$ has no almost peripheral vertices and $\operatorname{diam}(G\square H)$ is even, then

$$
\operatorname{aw}(G\square H,3)=3.
$$

Here $\operatorname{aw}(X,3)$ is the anti-van der Waerden number of $X$ with respect to $3$-term arithmetic progressions. The conjecture is proposed in the paper's future-work discussion as a condition guaranteeing the minimum possible value; no proof or counterexample is supplied.
technical_disposition: Anti-van der Waerden value for every qualifying Cartesian product requires exact graph arithmetic-progression conventions. Formula diam(u,v) in the description is ambiguous; eccentricity sum alone does not force rainbow triples. No full route.

statement_utf8:
Let $d\geqslant3$ and let $\Lambda$ be a full-rank lattice in $\mathbb{R}^d$. Its norm minimum is

$$
N(\Lambda)=\inf_{\mathbf{z}\in\Lambda\setminus\{\mathbf{0}\}}\Pi(\mathbf{z})^d.
$$

A lattice is called **algebraic** when it satisfies the algebraic-lattice condition referred to in the source. A diagonal operator is non-degenerate when its diagonal entries are nonzero.

**Cassels–Swinnerton-Dyer's conjecture.** The condition $N(\Lambda)>0$ is equivalent to the existence of a non-degenerate diagonal operator $D$ such that $D\Lambda$ is an algebraic lattice.

This is described as an analogue of Oppenheim's conjecture for decomposable forms and is stated to imply Littlewood's conjecture. The source gives a counterexample in dimension $2$ and leaves the assertion for $d\geqslant3$ as the conjectural case.
technical_disposition: For all d>=3 lattices, positive product minimum must imply diagonal algebraicity. Dimension-two counterexamples are outside scope; no classification mechanism and no low-burden certificate.

statement_utf8:
A signed graph $\hat{G}$ may have loops and parallel edges, and its balanced chromatic number $\chi_b(\hat{G})$ is the minimum number of parts in a partition of its vertices such that no part induces a negative cycle; negative loops are excluded when considering balanced colorings. Let $\tilde{K}_t$ be the signed graph obtained from $K_t$ by replacing every edge with one positive and one negative parallel edge. **Signed Hadwiger conjecture.** Every signed graph $\hat{G}$ with

$$
\chi_b(\hat{G})\geq t
$$

has a $\tilde{K}_t$-minor.

The paper proposes this as an intermediary signed version of Hadwiger's conjecture, and proves that it is equivalent to the ordinary Hadwiger conjecture through the parameter identity $M(t)=SM(t)$. Its relation to the odd Hadwiger conjecture is also established, but no resolution of the conjecture is stated.
technical_disposition: Universal signed-minor assertion has a stated equivalence to ordinary Hadwiger. Special t or a signed-to-ordinary reduction is not a resolution; no route to the full unbounded-t assertion.

statement_utf8:
Let $\phi:\Gamma\to\Lambda$ be a group homomorphism. The LS-category of the homomorphism, $\operatorname{cat}(\phi)$, is the minimum number $k$ such that a classifying-space map inducing $\phi$ can be covered by $k+1$ open sets on which its restrictions are nullhomotopic. The cohomological dimension $\operatorname{cd}(\phi)$ is the maximum $k$ for which there exists a $\mathbb{Z}\Lambda$-module $M$ such that the induced map

$$
\phi^*:H^k(\Lambda,M)\to H^k(\Gamma,M)
$$

is nonzero.

**Grant's LS-category conjecture.** For any group homomorphism $\phi:\Gamma\to\Lambda$,

$$
\operatorname{cat}(\phi)=\operatorname{cd}(\phi).
$$

This conjecture extends the Eilenberg–Ganea equality from groups to homomorphisms. The inequality $\operatorname{cd}(\phi)\leq\operatorname{cat}(\phi)$ is known in general, but the proposed equality is false: Tom Goodwillie gave a counterexample consisting of an epimorphism from an infinitely generated group to $\mathbb{Z}^2$ with $\operatorname{cd}(\phi)=1$.
technical_disposition: Literal statement already attributes a counterexample to Goodwillie with cd=1 and target Z squared. Primary construction not fetched, so HOLD on body verification, and no proposal to claim the reported example as new.

statement_utf8:
Let $H$ be a bipartite graph that is not a forest. Write $f(r,H)$ for the least integer $k$ such that every $H$-free $(r,k)$-graph does not exist, and write $\operatorname{ex}(N,H)$ for the maximum number of edges in an $H$-free graph on $N$ vertices. An $H$-free $(r,k)$-graph is a graph whose vertex set is partitioned into $r$ parts of size at most $k$, with at least one edge between every two parts. **Axenovich–Martin conjecture.** There is a positive constant $c=c(H)$ such that for any positive integers $r$ and $k$ satisfying

$$
\operatorname{ex}(rk,H)>c\binom{r}{2},
$$

there is an $H$-free $(r,k)$-graph, equivalently $f(r,H)<k$. If true, this would show that the trivial lower bound gives the correct order of magnitude and remove the logarithmic factor from the known upper bound for $f(r,H)$.
technical_disposition: All r,k and each nonforest bipartite H require the extremal-to-partition implication. Random partitioning without eliminating the logarithmic loss is inadequate; no complete mechanism. Definition of f in prose also needs source checking.

statement_utf8:
A singular harmonic map is associated with a collection of $N>1$ distinct punctures on the $z$-axis, at positions $\mathbf{z}=(z_1,\ldots,z_N)$, with potential constants giving nonzero angular momenta $\mathcal{J}_i$ at each puncture. The tangent map parameters are denoted by $b_i$, for $i=1,\ldots,N$.

**Extreme black hole uniqueness conjecture.** At least one tangent map parameter must be nonzero:

$$
\text{there exists }i\in\{1,\ldots,N\}\text{ such that }b_i\neq 0.
$$

This is a PDE formulation of the claim that regular asymptotically flat multiple degenerate black hole solutions to the axisymmetric stationary vacuum Einstein equations do not exist. If all $b_i$ vanished, the associated stationary vacuum spacetime would have no conical singularities and would provide a counterexample to extreme black hole uniqueness.
technical_disposition: All N>1 puncture collections with nonzero angular momenta must force some nonzero tangent parameter. A symmetric N=2 calculation or generic perturbation does not exclude every balanced singular harmonic map; no route.

statement_utf8:
Let $e_r(d,m;q)$ denote the maximum number of $\mathbb{F}_q$-rational points in the common zero set of an $r$-dimensional subspace of degree-$d$ homogeneous polynomials in $\mathbb{F}_q[x_0,dots,x_m]$. Let $H_j(d-1,m-l+1;q)$ and $pi_{m-l}(q)$ be defined as in the preceding notation. Suppose $m,d,r$ are positive integers satisfying $1\leq r\leq \binom{m+d}{d}$. Choose the unique $1\leq l\leq m+1$ such that

$$
\binom{m+d}{d}-\binom{m+d+1-l}{d}<r\leq\binom{m+d}{d}-\binom{m+d-l}{d}.
$$

Set $j=r-\binom{m+d}{d}+\binom{m+d+1-l}{d}$, so $0<j\leq\binom{m+d-l}{d-1}$. **Beelen-Datta-Ghorpade conjecture.** For $q\geq d+1$,

$$
e_r(d,m;q)=H_j(d-1,m-l+1;q)+\pi_{m-l}(q).
$$

This conjecture gives an exact formula for the generalized Hamming weights of projective Reed-Muller codes; the source proves it in the case $m=2$, while the general statement remains open.
technical_disposition: Primary Conjecture 1.1 matches q>=d+1 for all m,d,r. Theorems 1.3-1.4 give larger-field bounds and Theorem 1.5 addresses m=2; these do not fill all m>=3 and small q. No full route; known slices excluded.

statement_utf8:
Let $W(E_{10})$ be the Coxeter group under consideration, and let $\rho(d4e)$ denote the spectral radius of an element $d4e\in W(E_{10})$. For each level $n$, let $\Lambda_n\subset\mathbb{R}_{>1}$ be the set of spectral radii arising at $s_0$-level $n$, let $M_n$ and $m_n$ denote its maximal and minimal extreme values, and let $\hat\Lambda_n$ be the subset of primitive Salem numbers in $\Lambda_n$. **Spectral Growth Conjecture.** The maximal values satisfy

$$
M_n=M_1^n,\qquad n\geq 1,
$$

while the minimal extreme values approximately satisfy

$$
m_n\approx\delta^{n-2}M_{n-1},\qquad n\geq 3,
$$

for some $0<\delta<1$. Moreover,

$$
|\hat\Lambda_n|\sim C\cdot r^n,
$$

with $r\approx 5$, and the maximal gap between consecutive elements of $\hat\Lambda_n$ decays exponentially, so that the primitive spectrum becomes increasingly dense as $n\to\infty$. The approximation symbol indicates numerical proximity. These claims describe the experimentally observed spectral hierarchy in $W(E_{10})$: the exact formula for $M_n$ is proved in the source, while the scaling, exponential counting law, and density assertion remain conjectural.
technical_disposition: Composite target includes exact maxima, approximate minima, exponential counting and gap decay. Approximate notation lacks a quantitative tolerance, and maxima are reported already proved. No correction or single-clause proof credited; definitions/prior HOLD.

statement_utf8:
Let $V_{\boldsymbol{\Lambda}}=V_{\boldsymbol{\Lambda}^1}\otimes\dots\otimes V_{\boldsymbol{\Lambda}^k}$ be the tensor product of the relevant $\mathfrak g$-modules. Let $z^0$ have distinct coordinates, let $t^0$ be a non-degenerate critical point of the master function $\Phi(\cdot,z^0,\boldsymbol{\Lambda},\boldsymbol l)$, and let $t=t(z)$ be its locally continued non-degenerate critical point. Denote by $\omega(t(z),z)\in\operatorname{Sing}V_{\boldsymbol{\Lambda}}[\boldsymbol{\Lambda}-\alpha(\boldsymbol l)]$ the corresponding Bethe vector, and let $S$ be the tensor Shapovalov form. The norm formula gives

$$
S(\omega(t(z),z),\omega(t(z),z))=C\,\operatorname{Hess}_t\log\Phi(t(z),z,\boldsymbol{\Lambda},\boldsymbol l),
$$

where $C$ is independent of $z$. **Norm-constant conjecture.** The constant $C$ in this formula is equal to $1$. The conjecture specifies the normalization in the norm–Hessian identity for Bethe vectors. The cited theorem establishes the identity with an unspecified constant, while this statement proposes its exact value.
technical_disposition: All nondegenerate master-function critical points and normalization of Bethe vectors are essential. A rank-one check or rescaling cannot prove the norm-Hessian constant universally; likely substantial successor literature, unread. No new route.

statement_utf8:
Let $n$ and $l$ be positive integers, and let $X^{(l)}_{
u}(\rho)$, $X^{(l)'}_{
u}(\rho)$, $F^{(l)}_{
u}(q)$, and $F^{(l)'}_{
u}(q)$ denote the restricted one-dimensional sums and fermionic expressions defined above. For a partition $
u$, write $|
u|$ for its size and $
u_1$ for its largest part. **Fermionic formula conjecture.** For a partition $
u$ such that $|
u|\equiv 0\pmod n$ and $
u_1\le l$, and for a partition $\rho$ such that $\rho_1\le n-1$ and $|\rho|\equiv0\pmod n$, one has

X^{(l)}_{\nu}(l\Lambda_0)=F^{(l)}_{\nu}(q),\qquad X^{(l)'}_{\rho}(l\Lambda_0)=F^{(l)'}_{\rho}(q).
$$

These identities assert fermionic expressions for the restricted one-dimensional sums in the vacuum-module case; the source subsequently uses the first identity as an assumption in deriving further results.

statement_utf8:
Let $A$ and $B$ be finite-dimensional algebras over a field $K$, with all modules finitely generated right modules. The algebras are **derived equivalent** if their bounded derived categories of finitely generated modules are equivalent. An algebra is a **Morita algebra** if it has dominant dimension at least two and a minimal faithful projective-injective right module $eA$ such that $eAe$ is selfinjective.

**Chen–Xi's conjecture.** Suppose two algebras $A$ and $B$ are derived equivalent. If $A$ is a Morita algebra and the dominant dimension of $B$ is at least two, then $B$ is also a Morita algebra.

The conjecture concerns whether the Morita-algebra property is preserved in this one-sided form under derived equivalence. The paper's abstract states that the authors construct a counterexample, so the conjecture is refuted.
technical_disposition: Primary named theorem gives A Nakayama with Kupisch [4,5,4,5] and M=e0A+e1A+e3A+e1A/e1J^4; End_A(M) has dominant dimension 4 and is not Morita, while M tilting makes it derived equivalent. Lemmas 1.1-1.2 local proofs inspected. Existing counterexample defeats eligibility; full End algebra/dependency audit not claimed.

statement_utf8:
Let $\kappa$ be an algebraically closed field, and let $S_d(m,\kappa)$ be the degree-$d$ graded component of $\kappa[x_0,\dots,x_m]$. For $m\leq r\leq \binom{d+m}{m}$, define

$$
u_r(d,m):=\max\{|V(W)|:W\subseteq S_d(m,\kappa),\ \dim(W)=r,\ \dim(V(W))=0\}.
$$

Let

$$
\Omega'(d,m):=\Big\{(\alpha_1,\alpha_2,\dots,\alpha_{m+1})\in\mathbb{N}_0^{m+1}:\sum_{i=1}^{m+1}\alpha_i=d,\ d\notin\{\alpha_2,\dots,\alpha_m\}\Big\}.
$$

Order $\Omega'(d,m)$ lexicographically, let $\omega'_r(d,m)$ be its $r$th largest element, and, if $\omega'_r(d,m)=(\alpha_1,\dots,\alpha_{m+1})$, define

$$
H'_r(d,m):=\alpha_1d^{m-1}+\dots+\alpha_m.
$$

**Zero-dimensional intersection conjecture.** Given $d,m\geq 1$ and $m\leq r\leq \binom{d+m}{m}$, we have

$$
u_r(d,m)=H'_{r-(m-1)}(d,m).
$$

This conjecture proposes an exact formula for the largest possible cardinality of a zero-dimensional common vanishing set of an $r$-dimensional space of degree-$d$ forms. The supplied text does not establish the conjecture or give evidence resolving it; its status is therefore open.
technical_disposition: Primary source conjectures all d,m,r but proves the planar case. Bezout bound handles r=m, not the entire lex-index profile; no all-dimensional compression or counterexample. Empty-locus/endpoint conventions require source care, not correction credit.

statement_utf8:
Conjecture 9.1 proposes the identity

$$\left.\Theta_{e_r}\Theta_{e_k}\nabla e_{n-r-k}\right\rvert_{q=1}=\sum_{P\in\mathsf{LD}(0,n)^{\ast k,\circ r}}t^{\mathsf{area}(P)}x^P,$$

where $\mathsf{LD}(0,n)^{\ast k,\circ r}$ is the set of positively labelled Dyck paths of size $n$ with $k$ decorated rises and $r$ decorated contractible valleys.
technical_disposition: Mixed decorated rises and contractible valleys at q=1 require the precise Theta/nabla normalization and all n,r,k. Known pure-decoration identities do not automatically give the mixed formula; no full route.
